Four reverts: (1) bot/src/wizard.js stepPrompt 'source' case — the 'Reply to this message with the source ... plain sends and forwards cannot be matched to this wizard' text and its 5-line phase-5-sweep comment block are replaced by the legacy 'Send or forward the video, or paste a direct link / Google Drive link / magnet URI / public t.me channel-post link, or upload a .torrent file (<= 1 MB).'; (2) bot/src/index.js handleMessage video/document reject branch — 'This file was not sent as a reply, so it cannot be matched to a flow ... reply to the step-1 prompt' restored to the legacy 'This video was not expected. wrong_fix_reverted.what_was_rewritten_instead_of_deleted: TWO things were deliberately KEPT/REWRITTEN rather than reverted. (a) The message.audio branch that 8f9e46e ADDED to handleMessage is structurally useful and is KEPT: before it, a bare (non-reply) audio fell through to showHome SILENTLY, which is a genuine defect independent of the reply-vs-bare-send question. Only its reply-only guidance text was reverted; it now reads 'This audio file was not expected. Open Settings -> Music library and tap Add music files, then send or forward the tracks.' (b) bot/test/flow-forward-regression.test.mjs was REWRITTEN, not deleted: its 5 tests pinned the WRONG (reply-only) behavior, so the copy assertions are inverted to pin the RESTORED send-or-forward copy, and the file grew to 6 tests. While rewriting, a real HARNESS BUG in the 8f9e46e version was found and fixed: its genuine-reply test ('a .torrent REPLY ... routes to the wizard') seeded NO credentials, so handleTorrentDocument's requireCredentials() returned falsy, handleFlowReply returned undefined, and the message actually fell through to the reject branch — the test passed only vacuously because the OLD reject copy happened not to contain the string 'not expected' that it asserted against. It never verified reply routing at all. The rewritten harness seeds credentials via putCredentials (as tasks.test.mjs does) and stubs the Telegram getFile/file-download and the GitHub contents PUT, so the reply path is now genuinely exercised end to end and a second genuine-reply test (text/link reply) was added alongside it.

design_confirmation.write_frequency_reasoning: CONFIRMED SAFE. The kv-minimization migration removed the legacy per-chat state blob because it was rewritten on EVERY navigation event (menus, wizards, per-keystroke-equivalent updates). The awaiting_input marker is written ONLY when the bot sends a force_reply/flow-marker prompt: one INSERT OR REPLACE per prompt-sent (a user-initiated step transition), one SELECT per bare non-command message, and one conditional DELETE per consumed marker. Prompt sends are a strict subset of the old navigation writes (menus never write awaiting_input at all), and there is no per-message write path — bare input messages only read. Volume is bounded at one write per input step per chat, far below the removed blob's write rate. IMPLEMENTED as designed: the ONLY write path is the sendForceReply choke point (one upsert per prompt-sent) plus a direct re-anchor on the uplb indicator in-place-edit path (one upsert per pasted fragment — same order as the prompt traffic it mirrors). The uplb indicator EDIT is not a sendForceReply call, so the choke point cannot see it; that path re-anchors explicitly with the new buffer token or a bare next fragment would lose earlier fragments.
design_confirmation.precedence_rule_implemented: IMPLEMENTED in handleMessage (index.js): parseFlowReply is checked FIRST; the awaiting_input lookup runs ONLY inside `if (!flowReply)`. A genuine reply to an older prompt therefore always wins over a newer awaiting_input row — the reply is the more specific, explicit user signal.

step 2: 0002_awaiting_input.sql (chat_id PK, op, payload, expires_at) + storage.js putAwaitingInput/getAwaitingInput/deleteAwaitingInput with AWAITING_INPUT_TTL_SECONDS=900 (15 min; RELAY_TTL_SECONDS 12h is a relay-handoff convention, rejected as too long) + d1.mjs test helper now loads ALL migrations/*.sql in filename order (was 0001 only)

step 3: core mechanism. (a) sendForceReply choke point (telegram.js): derives the cf: marker arithmetically from its own outgoing text and upserts awaiting_input, failure non-fatal. (b) handleMessage read path: bare send/forward routes via awaiting_input -> handleFlowReply (same handlers, no fork); payload-conditional consume-delete (deleteAwaitingInputIfUnconsumed) leaves a re-anchored next-step row intact, clears a completed one. (c) routeCallback pre-dispatch prune makes ALL button completions/cancels safe uniformly. (d) explicit clears on wizard cancel, startJob completion, /cancel. (e) uplb indicator-edit re-anchor. Precedence: reply edge checked first, awaiting_input only when no reply.

Genuine-reply pins in flow-forward-regression.test.mjs untouched. Also fixed a real bug the tests caught: deleteAwaitingInputIfUnconsumed was missing from the index.js storage import. 191/191 pass.

human_review_items: The 8f9e46e genuine-reply test was passing VACUOUSLY (no credentials seeded => fell through to the reject branch, asserted against a string the old copy did not contain). Fixed here. Worth checking whether other suites share the same no-credentials harness shape and are therefore also asserting less than they appear to.

The multi-bubble production.json fragment guidance in beginPlanUpload ('reply the first fragment to this prompt, then reply each following fragment to the receiving indicator') is intentionally PRESERVED — it predates 8f9e46e and describes the uplb fragment-chaining mechanism, which is a genuine reply-edge design, not the wrong fix. Once awaiting_input lands, revisit whether multi-bubble pastes can also be recognised without the reply edge (the uplb buffer currently rides the indicator message's marker, so this needs its own thought).

bot/src/index.js and bot/src/github.js contain a literal control character inside a regex literal (SAFE_AUDIO_FILENAME_RE), which makes git and grep treat them as binary. Diffs for these files show as 'Bin ... bytes differ'. Use `grep --text`. Not introduced by this session; flagged because it makes review of index.js changes harder.

routeCallback now prunes awaiting_input before EVERY callback dispatch. Verified safe: every callback that starts/continues an input flow sends its own force_reply prompt (choke point re-marks), so the prune only ever removes stale markers. This is what makes ml:uploaddone, the music batch's set:music cancel, and wizard navigation uniformly safe without per-callback clears. If a future callback ever continues an input flow WITHOUT sending a fresh prompt, this assumption breaks — the uplb indicator-edit path is the one current example and has its own explicit re-anchor.

Test suite seeds awaiting_input rows directly via putAwaitingInput for the routing/expiry/precedence tests; the choke-point WRITE path (prompt sent -> row appears) gets an end-to-end test in step 5 (drive /new and assert the wzs row exists).
